disclosures.name: TestAlloc/Info
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: the variadic `...any` argument list boxes each value into a heap shell where Go's interface value is two words carrying the data pointer inline (DESIGN-iface-shell-caching §2 — 'C# has no two-word interface value; the shell IS the itab+data fused into an object')

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/Error
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: same `...any` boxing as TestAlloc/Info on the Error level path — one heap shell per argument where Go's interface value allocates nothing

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/logger.Info
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: the Logger.Info convenience path boxes its `...any` arguments into heap shells where Go passes two-word interface values

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/logger.Log
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: the Logger.Log path boxes its `...any` arguments into heap shells where Go passes two-word interface values

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/pairs
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: each key/value pair boxes through `any` into a heap shell; Go's escape analysis keeps the equivalent interface values off the heap entirely

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/2_pairs
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert with a NONZERO Go budget (2): the managed model pays a heap shell per boxed pair on top of Go's two budgeted allocations, so the divergence is the shell count rather than the assert's premise

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/2_pairs_disabled_inline
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert with a nonzero Go budget: even on the level-disabled path the `...any` arguments are boxed before the level check can discard them, where Go's interface values cost nothing to form

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/9_kvs
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert with a nonzero Go budget (10): nine key/value pairs box into nine heap shells above Go's budgeted slice growth

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/attrs1
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: constructing one Attr materializes a boxed Value in the managed model where Go's Value packs the payload into its own struct fields

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/attrs3
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: three Attrs, each carrying a boxed Value shell that Go's packed Value representation does not allocate

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/attrs3_disabled
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: the Attrs are constructed — and therefore boxed — before the level check discards them, so the level-disabled path allocates in the managed model exactly as the enabled one does

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/attrs6
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert with a nonzero Go budget (1): six Attrs box six Values above Go's single budgeted allocation

disclosures.name: TestAlloc/attrs9
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert with a nonzero Go budget (1): nine Attrs box nine Values above Go's single budgeted allocation

disclosures.name: TestAnyLevelAlloc
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: passing a Level through `any` boxes the value type into a heap shell, which is precisely the allocation Go's two-word interface value avoids

disclosures.name: TestTextHandlerAlloc
disclosures.reason: wantAllocs assert: TextHandler.Handle formats through boxed Values and an interface-typed Handler, so the append-only formatting path Go performs allocation-free pays one heap shell per attribute here

disclosures.name: TestAttrNoAlloc
disclosures.reason: want-zero AllocsPerRun assert: each Attr constructor boxes its payload into a Value shell in the managed model, where Go's Value stores the payload inline in the struct and allocates nothing

disclosures.name: TestValueNoAlloc
disclosures.reason: want-zero AllocsPerRun assert: every Value constructor boxes through `any` into a heap shell, the direct managed counterpart of Go's inline-payload Value (DESIGN-iface-shell-caching §2 — the shell IS the interface value, and nothing short of IDynamicInterfaceCastable removes it)
